name: Classes
description: Classes refers to an object-oriented programming construct that defines the attributes/state and operations/behaviour shared by objects of the class. In Foundations & Linear Data Structures, the focus is on class definitions, objects/instances, attributes, methods, encapsulation, abstraction, constructors, visibility and implementation of abstract data types.
:LABEL: Subtopic

name: Stacks
description: Stacks refers to a linear abstract data type in which insertion and deletion occur at one designated end, following last-in-first-out (LIFO) order. In Foundations & Linear Data Structures, the focus is on push, pop, peek/top, underflow/overflow conditions, array- and linked implementations, and time/space complexity.
:LABEL: Subtopic

name: Queues
description: Queues refers to a linear abstract data type in which insertion is performed at one end and deletion at the other, following first-in-first-out (FIFO) order. In Linear Data Structures, the focus is on enqueue, dequeue, front/rear operations, circular queues, array/linked implementations, and underflow/overflow conditions.
:LABEL: Subtopic

name: Linked Lists
description: Linked Lists refers to a linked linear data structure consisting of nodes that contain data and one or more links to other nodes. In Linear Data Structures, the focus is on singly, doubly and circular lists; insertion/deletion; traversal; node references.
:LABEL: Subtopic

name: Binary Search Tree (BST)
description: Binary Search Tree (BST) refers to a binary tree in which keys in the left subtree are ordered relative to the node key and keys in the right subtree are ordered in the opposite direction, according to the chosen ordering rule. In Trees & Graphs, the focus is on search, insertion, deletion, traversal, ordering invariant, height and best/average/worst-case complexity.
:LABEL: Subtopic

name: AVL Trees
description: AVL Trees refers to a self-balancing binary search tree in which the height difference between the left and right subtrees of every node is bounded by one. In Trees & Graphs, the focus is on balance factor, rotations, insertion/deletion rebalancing, search and height guarantees.
:LABEL: Subtopic

name: Quick/Merge sort
description: Quick/Merge sort: Comparison-based sorting methods represented here by Quicksort and Mergesort, which organize elements into sorted order using divide-and-conquer strategies. In Sorting & Searching, the focus is on partitioning and recursive subproblems in Quicksort; splitting and merging in Mergesort; stability, in-place behaviour and time/space complexity.
:LABEL: Subtopic

name: Binary Search
description: Binary Search refers to a search algorithm that repeatedly compares a target with the middle element of an ordered sequence and eliminates half of the remaining search interval. In Sorting & Searching, the focus is on sorted data requirement, iterative/recursive implementation, interval reduction and complexity.
:LABEL: Subtopic

name: Collision resolution
description: Collision resolution: Techniques used in hash tables to handle multiple keys that map to the same table location. In Hashing, the focus is on separate chaining, open addressing, probing strategies, load factor and clustering effects.
:LABEL: Subtopic

name: Truth tables
description: Truth tables refers to a tabular method for evaluating the truth value of a propositional or logical expression for every possible assignment of its component propositions. In Propositional Logic, the focus is on logical connectives, compound propositions, equivalence, tautology, contradiction and satisfiability checks.
:LABEL: Subtopic

name: Induction
description: Induction refers to a proof method in which a statement is established for an initial case and then shown to hold for the next case assuming it holds for the current case. In Proof Techniques, the focus is on weak/ordinary induction, strong induction, base case, inductive hypothesis and inductive step.
:LABEL: Subtopic

name: Equivalence relations
description: Equivalence relations refers to a binary relation that is reflexive, symmetric and transitive, thereby partitioning a set into equivalence classes. In Set Theory & Relations, the focus is on relation properties, equivalence classes, partitions and representative elements.
:LABEL: Subtopic

name: Pigeonhole principle
description: Pigeonhole principle refers to a counting principle stating that placing more objects than containers into those containers forces at least one container to contain more than one object. In Combinatorics, the focus is on basic and generalized forms, counting arguments and existence proofs.
:LABEL: Subtopic

name: Trees
description: Trees refers to a connected acyclic graph used to represent hierarchical or recursive relationships. In Graph Theory, the focus is on rooted trees, parent/child relationships, degree, height, depth, traversal and common tree representations.
:LABEL: Subtopic

name: Entities, relationships & constraints
description: Entities, relationships & constraints: Core components of conceptual database modelling in which entities represent distinguishable objects, relationships represent associations, and constraints specify valid states. In ER Modeling, the focus is on entity sets, attributes, relationship sets, cardinality/participation constraints, keys and integrity constraints.
:LABEL: Subtopic

name: Relational algebra
description: Relational algebra refers to a formal procedural query language based on operations over relations, producing relations as results. In Relational Model, the focus is on selection, projection, union, difference, Cartesian product, joins, renaming and derived operations.
:LABEL: Subtopic

name: SQL queries
description: SQL queries: Declarative statements used to define, retrieve, manipulate and control data in relational database systems. In SQL, the focus is on sELECT queries, filtering, joins, grouping, aggregation, subqueries and data modification statements.
:LABEL: Subtopic

name: Boyce-Codd Normal Form
description: Boyce-Codd Normal Form refers to a relational normal form in which every determinant of a non-trivial functional dependency is a superkey. In Normalization, the focus is on functional dependencies, candidate keys, determinants, decomposition and lossless/dependency-preserving considerations.
:LABEL: Subtopic

name: Concurrency control
description: Concurrency control: Database mechanisms that coordinate concurrent transactions so that their interleaved execution preserves required correctness properties. In Transaction Management, the focus is on serializability, locking, timestamps, isolation, conflicts, deadlock interaction and recovery considerations.
:LABEL: Subtopic

name: Deadlocks
description: Deadlocks refers to a state in which a set of processes or threads are permanently blocked because each waits for a resource or event held or controlled by another member of the set. In Processes, the focus is on necessary conditions, resource-allocation graphs, prevention, avoidance, detection and recovery.
:LABEL: Subtopic

name: Thread synchronization
description: Thread synchronization: Coordination mechanisms that control the ordering and mutual access of concurrent threads to shared state. In Threads & Synchronization, the focus is on critical sections, mutexes/locks, semaphores, monitors, condition variables, race conditions and atomicity.
:LABEL: Subtopic

name: Scheduling algorithms
description: Scheduling algorithms: Algorithms used by an operating system to select processes or threads for execution and allocate processor time. In CPU Scheduling, the focus is on fCFS, SJF/SRTF, priority, round-robin and multilevel scheduling; response, waiting and turnaround metrics.
:LABEL: Subtopic

name: Paging and virtual memory
description: Paging and virtual memory: Memory-management techniques that divide address spaces into pages and physical memory into frames, allowing virtual addresses to be mapped to physical locations. In Memory Management, the focus is on page tables, address translation, page faults, demand paging, replacement and working-set considerations.
:LABEL: Subtopic

name: File allocation and organization
description: File allocation and organization: Methods by which an operating system organizes files and allocates storage blocks to represent their contents. In File Systems, the focus is on contiguous, linked and indexed allocation, directories, free-space management and access patterns.
:LABEL: Subtopic

name: Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU)
description: Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU) refers to the arithmetic logic unit is a processor datapath component that performs arithmetic, logical and related bitwise operations on operands. In Digital Logic, the focus is on arithmetic operations, logical operations, flags/status outputs, operand width and datapath integration.
:LABEL: Subtopic

name: Reduced Instruction Set Computer / Complex Instruction Set Computer (RISC/CISC)
description: RISC/CISC: Two broad instruction-set design approaches distinguished by how instruction complexity, encoding, addressing and implementation responsibilities are organized. In Instruction Set Architecture, the focus is on instruction complexity, instruction formats, addressing modes, register use, code density and implementation trade-offs.
:LABEL: Subtopic

name: Pipeline hazards
description: Pipeline hazards: Conditions in a pipelined processor that prevent the next instruction from proceeding through the pipeline as scheduled. In Pipelining, the focus is on structural, data and control hazards; stalls, forwarding, scheduling and branch handling.
:LABEL: Subtopic

name: Caches and virtual memory
description: Caches and virtual memory: Memory-hierarchy mechanisms that exploit locality: caches retain frequently used data near processors, while virtual memory maps virtual addresses to physical storage. In Memory Hierarchy, the focus is on cache levels, locality, mapping, replacement, write policies, TLBs and page translation.
:LABEL: Subtopic

name: I/O organization and interfaces
description: I/O organization and interfaces: Processor and system mechanisms used to communicate with peripheral devices and external interfaces. In I/O Systems, the focus is on programmed I/O, interrupts, DMA, buses, device controllers and interface protocols.
:LABEL: Subtopic

name: Merge sort
description: Merge sort refers to a stable comparison-based sorting algorithm that recursively divides a sequence and merges sorted sub-sequences. In Divide & Conquer, the focus is on divide-and-conquer decomposition, merge operation, stability and auxiliary storage.
:LABEL: Subtopic

name: Knapsack
description: Knapsack refers to a family of optimization problems that selects items under a capacity constraint to maximize total value. In Dynamic Programming, the focus is on for 0/1 knapsack, each item is selected at most once; state formulation, recurrence, dynamic programming and capacity/value constraints.
:LABEL: Subtopic

name: Activity selection
description: Activity selection refers to a scheduling problem that selects a maximum-size subset of mutually compatible activities given start and finish times. In Greedy Algorithms, the focus is on compatibility, earliest-finish-time greedy rule, selection sequence and proof of optimality.
:LABEL: Subtopic

name: Network flow
description: Network flow refers to a graph-based optimization model in which flow is sent through directed edges subject to capacity constraints from a source toward a sink. In Graph Algorithms, the focus is on flow conservation, capacities, residual networks, augmenting paths, max-flow/min-cut and common algorithms.
:LABEL: Subtopic

name: NP-complete problems
description: NP-complete problems: Decision problems that are both in NP and NP-hard, meaning every problem in NP can be polynomial-time reduced to them. In NP-Completeness, the focus is on polynomial verification, polynomial-time reductions, NP-hardness and representative problems.
:LABEL: Subtopic

name: Process models
description: Process models: Structured approaches for organizing software development activities, deliverables and control points across a development lifecycle. In Software Development Life Cycle, the focus is on waterfall, iterative/incremental, spiral, agile and hybrid lifecycle approaches; activities, feedback and change management.
:LABEL: Subtopic

name: Continuous integration and delivery
description: Continuous integration and delivery: Software engineering practices that automate frequent integration, verification and delivery of software changes through a controlled pipeline. In Agile & Scrum, the focus is on build automation, version control integration, automated tests, artifact management, deployment automation and release controls.
:LABEL: Subtopic

name: Use cases and requirements specification
description: Use cases and requirements specification: Techniques for eliciting, documenting and validating required system behaviour, qualities and constraints from stakeholder needs. In Requirements Engineering, the focus is on functional/non-functional requirements, actors, use cases, scenarios, acceptance criteria, traceability and validation.
:LABEL: Subtopic

name: Design patterns
description: Design patterns: Reusable, named design solutions to recurring software design problems within a stated context and set of trade-offs. In System Design, the focus is on creational, structural and behavioural patterns; participants, collaborations, consequences and applicability.
:LABEL: Subtopic

name: Unit and integration testing
description: Unit and integration testing: Testing practices that verify individual software units and their interactions with collaborating components. In Software Testing, the focus is on test cases, fixtures, mocks/stubs, unit boundaries, integration strategies, interfaces and defect isolation.
:LABEL: Subtopic

name: Transmission media and signalling
description: Transmission media and signalling: Physical means and signalling methods used to carry information across a communication channel. In Physical Layer, the focus is on copper, fibre and wireless media; bandwidth, attenuation, noise, modulation/encoding and transmission characteristics.
:LABEL: Subtopic

name: Framing and MAC
description: Framing and MAC: Data-link mechanisms that delimit frames and control access to a shared or point-to-point communication medium. In Data Link Layer, the focus is on frame structure, error detection, MAC addressing, Ethernet, collision handling and medium-access methods.
:LABEL: Subtopic

name: IP addressing and routing
description: IP addressing and routing: Network-layer mechanisms for identifying interfaces or endpoints and selecting paths for forwarding packets between networks. In Network Layer, the focus is on iPv4/IPv6 addressing, subnetting, forwarding tables, routing principles and route selection.
:LABEL: Subtopic

name: Transmission Control Protocol / User Datagram Protocol (TCP/UDP)
description: TCP/UDP: Transport-layer protocols represented by TCP, a connection-oriented reliable byte-stream protocol, and UDP, a connectionless datagram transport. In Transport Layer, the focus is on ports, multiplexing, TCP sequencing/acknowledgement/congestion control and UDP datagrams.
:LABEL: Subtopic

name: Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP)
description: Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP) refers to an application-layer request/response protocol used for transferring web resources and related representations. In Application Layer, the focus is on methods, status codes, headers, message semantics, caching, persistent connections and HTTP over secure transports.
:LABEL: Subtopic

name: Hooke's Law
description: Hooke's Law: Within the linear elastic range of a material, stress is proportional to strain for the relevant loading mode. In Simple Stresses, the focus is on normal stress/strain relation, elastic modulus, proportional limit and applicability to linear elasticity.
:LABEL: Subtopic

name: Flexure formula
description: Flexure formula refers to the beam flexure relation that connects bending stress to bending moment, cross-sectional geometry and distance from the neutral axis under stated beam assumptions. In Bending Moment, the focus is on σ = My/I, neutral axis, second moment of area, bending moment and elastic-beam assumptions.
:LABEL: Subtopic

name: Bending stress distribution
description: Bending stress distribution refers to the spatial variation of normal bending stress across a beam cross-section caused by an applied bending moment. In Bending Stresses, the focus is on linear stress distribution in elastic homogeneous sections, neutral axis, extreme fibres and section modulus.
:LABEL: Subtopic

name: Circular shafts
description: Circular shafts: Cylindrical structural members designed to transmit torque and resist associated torsional stresses and deformation. In Torsion, the focus is on solid/hollow shafts, torque, polar moment of inertia, torsional shear stress, angle of twist and power transmission.
:LABEL: Subtopic

name: Beam deflection methods
description: Beam deflection methods: Analytical methods used to determine displacement and slope of beams under transverse loading. In Deflection, the focus is on double integration, singularity functions, moment-area, conjugate beam and related elastic methods.
:LABEL: Subtopic

name: Viscosity
description: Viscosity refers to a measure of a fluid’s resistance to deformation and flow, arising from internal friction and relating shear stress to velocity gradient under Newtonian conditions. In Fluid Properties, the focus is on concept-level scope: the defining mechanism, properties, constraints, and application criteria; curricular context is recorded in Concept_Category and Typical_Modules.
:LABEL: Subtopic

name: Buoyancy
description: Buoyancy refers to the net upward force exerted by a fluid on an immersed or floating body due to the pressure distribution in the fluid. In Hydrostatics, the focus is on archimedes' principle, displaced-fluid volume, centre of buoyancy and floating equilibrium.
:LABEL: Subtopic

name: Continuity
description: Continuity refers to the mass-conservation relation requiring that mass entering, leaving and accumulating within a fluid system satisfy conservation of mass. In Kinematics, the focus is on control-volume continuity, steady/unsteady flow, incompressible simplification and area-velocity relationships.
:LABEL: Subtopic

name: Reynolds number
description: Reynolds number refers to a dimensionless ratio comparing inertial effects with viscous effects in fluid flow. In Dynamics, the focus is on re = ρVL/μ, characteristic length/velocity choices, similarity and flow-regime interpretation.
:LABEL: Subtopic

name: Head loss and pipe-flow analysis
description: Head loss and pipe-flow analysis: Analysis of pressure or energy losses associated with fluid flow through pipes and fittings. In Pipe Flow, the focus is on darcy-Weisbach equation, friction factor, minor losses, hydraulic grade/energy lines and flow regimes.
:LABEL: Subtopic

name: Truss and beam analysis
description: Truss and beam analysis: Structural analysis procedures for determining internal forces and reactions in idealized trusses and beams under applied loads. In Determinate Structures, the focus is on equilibrium, free-body diagrams, axial truss forces, shear and bending moment in beams.
:LABEL: Subtopic

name: Moment-area theorem
description: Moment-area theorem: Beam-deflection relations that connect changes in slope and deflection to areas and first moments of the M/EI diagram. In Deflections, the focus is on theorem 1 for slope change, theorem 2 for tangential deviation, boundary conditions and sign conventions.
:LABEL: Subtopic

name: Virtual work
description: Virtual work refers to an analytical method that uses work equivalence under a compatible virtual displacement to determine structural responses. In Energy Methods, the focus is on virtual displacements, external/internal virtual work, unit-load method and displacement calculation.
:LABEL: Subtopic

name: Influence-line construction
description: Influence-line construction refers to a graphical or analytical representation showing how a response quantity at a specified location varies as a moving load changes position. In Influence Lines, the focus is on influence lines for reactions, shear, moment and other responses in determinate structures.
:LABEL: Subtopic

name: Slope-deflection
description: Slope-deflection refers to a displacement-based structural analysis method relating member end moments to end rotations, translations and fixed-end actions. In Indeterminate Structures, the focus is on member stiffness, end rotations, joint translations, fixed-end moments and compatibility equations.
:LABEL: Subtopic

name: Atterberg limits
description: Atterberg limits: Empirical moisture-content limits used to characterize the consistency and plasticity range of fine-grained soils. In Soil Classification, the focus is on liquid limit, plastic limit, shrinkage limit, plasticity index and consistency states.
:LABEL: Subtopic

name: Darcy's law
description: Darcy's law refers to a constitutive relation stating that, under laminar saturated porous-media flow conditions, discharge is proportional to hydraulic gradient and hydraulic conductivity. In Permeability, the focus is on hydraulic head, gradient, hydraulic conductivity, discharge/flux and applicability limits.
:LABEL: Subtopic

name: Consolidation settlement
description: Consolidation settlement: Time-dependent settlement of a saturated or nearly saturated soil caused by dissipation of excess pore-water pressure and associated volume change under sustained loading. In Consolidation, the focus is on concept-level scope: the defining mechanism, properties, constraints, and application criteria; curricular context is recorded in Concept_Category and Typical_Modules.
:LABEL: Subtopic

name: Mohr-Coulomb failure criterion
description: Mohr-Coulomb failure criterion refers to a frictional failure criterion relating shear strength of soil or rock to effective normal stress, cohesion and friction angle. In Shear Strength, the focus is on τf = c' + σ'n tanφ' for effective-stress form, failure envelope and drained/undrained interpretation.
:LABEL: Subtopic

name: Lateral earth pressure
description: Lateral earth pressure refers to the pressure exerted by soil against a retaining or embedded structure due to soil self-weight, surcharge, groundwater and other actions. In Earth Pressure, the focus is on active, passive and at-rest states, earth-pressure coefficients, wall friction and groundwater effects.
:LABEL: Subtopic

name: Demand forecasting
description: Demand forecasting: Estimation of future demand for a resource or service from historical observations, explanatory variables, assumptions, and uncertainty, used to support planning and design. In Water Demand, the focus is on concept-level scope: the defining mechanism, properties, constraints, and application criteria; curricular context is recorded in Concept_Category and Typical_Modules.
:LABEL: Subtopic

name: Filtration
description: Filtration refers to a water or wastewater treatment process that removes suspended or particulate matter by passing fluid through a porous filter medium. In Water Treatment, the focus is on media filtration, straining, adsorption contributions, head loss, backwashing and filtration performance.
:LABEL: Subtopic

name: Sewer design
description: Sewer design: Engineering design of sewer systems to collect and convey wastewater safely and reliably to treatment or disposal facilities. In Wastewater Collection, the focus is on flow estimation, pipe sizing, hydraulic grade, self-cleansing considerations, minimum/maximum velocities and system layout.
:LABEL: Subtopic

name: Activated sludge process
description: Activated sludge process refers to a suspended-growth biological wastewater-treatment process in which microorganisms oxidize biodegradable pollutants in an aerated reactor followed by solids separation. In Sewage Treatment, the focus is on aeration, biomass concentration, substrate removal, secondary clarification, sludge age and return/waste activated sludge.
:LABEL: Subtopic

name: Solid-waste management
description: Solid-waste management refers to the systematic handling of solid wastes through generation reduction, segregation, collection, transport, processing, recovery and final disposal. In Solid Waste, the focus is on waste characterization, collection, recycling/material recovery, biological treatment, thermal treatment and engineered disposal.
:LABEL: Subtopic

name: Sight distance
description: Sight distance refers to the roadway length over which a driver can see an object or roadway feature sufficiently far ahead to perform a required manoeuvre safely. In Highway Planning, the focus is on stopping, passing and decision sight distance; driver perception-reaction, speed, grade and geometric constraints.
:LABEL: Subtopic

name: Super elevation
description: Super elevation refers to the transverse slope provided on a roadway curve to assist in counteracting lateral acceleration associated with vehicle motion. In Geometric Design, the focus is on superelevation rate, side friction, design speed, radius, runoff and transition.
:LABEL: Subtopic

name: Traffic flow and control
description: Traffic flow and control: Analysis and management of the movement of vehicles and people on transportation networks using flow relationships and control strategies. In Traffic Engineering, the focus is on flow, speed, density, fundamental diagrams, intersections, signals, capacity and control measures.
:LABEL: Subtopic

name: Bitumen testing
description: Bitumen testing: Laboratory characterization of bituminous binders through standardized tests of consistency, viscosity, temperature susceptibility and related properties. In Pavement Materials, the focus is on penetration, ductility, softening point, viscosity, flash/fire point and temperature susceptibility, as applicable to the specification.
:LABEL: Subtopic

name: Flexible pavement design
description: Flexible pavement design: Design of layered pavement systems in which wheel loads are distributed through bituminous and granular layers over the subgrade. In Pavement Design, the focus is on traffic loading, material properties, layer thicknesses, subgrade strength, drainage, fatigue and rutting considerations.
:LABEL: Subtopic

name: Gantt charts
description: Gantt charts refers to a time-scaled project scheduling representation showing activities, durations and their planned timing. In Project Lifecycle, the focus is on activities, durations, start/finish dates, overlaps, milestones and progress tracking.
:LABEL: Subtopic

name: Crashing
description: Crashing refers to a schedule-compression technique that reduces activity durations by applying additional resources or cost, subject to technical feasibility. In Network Techniques (CPM/PERT), the focus is on normal/crash durations and costs, cost slopes, critical paths and incremental time-cost trade-offs.
:LABEL: Subtopic

name: Resource levelling
description: Resource levelling refers to a scheduling process that adjusts activity timing to resolve resource over-allocation while respecting stated project constraints. In Resource Allocation, the focus is on resource availability, activity priorities, float, sequencing and schedule impacts.
:LABEL: Subtopic

name: Depreciation and cost control
description: Depreciation and cost control: Methods for allocating the depreciable cost of assets over their useful lives and monitoring project costs against budgets. In Cost Control, the focus is on straight-line and declining-balance methods, book value, useful life, residual value, cost variance and budget control.
:LABEL: Subtopic

name: Equipment selection and productivity
description: Equipment selection and productivity: Selection and operational assessment of construction equipment based on required work, capacity, cycle time, site conditions and economic constraints. In Construction Equipment, the focus is on equipment capacity, cycle time, utilization, production rate, operating cost and site compatibility.
:LABEL: Subtopic

name: Errors
description: Errors: Deviations of measured or computed quantities from an accepted reference or true/accepted value, including systematic and random components. In Basics of Surveying, the focus is on accuracy, precision, systematic/random error, propagation, uncertainty and error detection.
:LABEL: Subtopic

name: Benchmarks
description: Benchmarks: Reference points with known or established elevations used to control vertical surveying and transfer elevation information. In Leveling & Contouring, the focus is on permanent/temporary benchmarks, datum, reduced levels, levelling networks and monumentation.
:LABEL: Subtopic

name: Angular measurement
description: Angular measurement: Determination of horizontal or vertical angles between survey lines or directions using appropriate angular-measurement instruments. In Theodolite Surveying, the focus is on theodolites/total stations, centering, face observations, repetition, direction measurement and error control.
:LABEL: Subtopic

name: Horizontal and vertical curves
description: Horizontal and vertical curves: Geometric transition elements used to connect roadway alignments while controlling changes in direction and grade. In Curves, the focus is on simple/compound horizontal curves, circular elements, transition curves, vertical parabolic curves and sight-distance considerations.
:LABEL: Subtopic

name: GNSS/GPS and GIS applications
description: GNSS/GPS and GIS applications: Use of satellite-based positioning and geographic information systems to acquire, reference, manage, analyze and visualize spatial data. In Modern Surveying (GPS/GIS), the focus is on gNSS positioning, coordinate reference systems, accuracy/error sources, GIS layers, spatial queries and mapping.
:LABEL: Subtopic

name: Control volumes
description: Control volumes refers to a defined region in space used for applying conservation equations to mass, momentum, and energy crossing its boundary. In Basic Concepts, the focus is on concept-level scope: the defining mechanism, properties, constraints, and application criteria; curricular context is recorded in Concept_Category and Typical_Modules.
:LABEL: Subtopic

name: Energy equation
description: Energy equation refers to a statement of energy conservation applied to a thermodynamic system or control volume. In First Law, the focus is on internal, kinetic and potential energy, heat transfer, work, mass-flow energy and steady-flow simplifications.
:LABEL: Subtopic

name: Second-law analysis
description: Second-law analysis: Thermodynamic analysis based on the second law, including entropy balance and restrictions on energy-conversion processes. In Second Law, the focus is on entropy balance, irreversibility, entropy generation, reversible/irreversible processes and efficiency limits.
:LABEL: Subtopic

name: Entropy generation
description: Entropy generation refers to the production of entropy associated with irreversible processes within a system or control volume. In Entropy, the focus is on entropy balance, heat transfer across finite temperature differences, friction, mixing and other irreversibilities.
:LABEL: Subtopic

name: Carnot cycle
description: Carnot cycle refers to an ideal reversible heat-engine cycle consisting of two isothermal and two reversible adiabatic (isentropic) processes between two thermal reservoirs. In Gas Power Cycles, the focus is on isothermal expansion/compression, isentropic expansion/compression and maximum reversible efficiency.
:LABEL: Subtopic

name: Velocity and acceleration fields
description: Velocity and acceleration fields: Spatial and temporal fields describing fluid-particle velocity and acceleration throughout a flow domain. In Fluid Kinematics, the focus is on eulerian velocity field, material acceleration, local and convective acceleration, streamlines.
:LABEL: Subtopic

name: Navier-Stokes equation
description: Navier-Stokes equation refers to the momentum-conservation equation for a continuum fluid, with terms determined by density, pressure, body forces and constitutive behaviour. In Conservation Laws, the focus is on continuity coupling, pressure, viscous stresses, body forces, incompressible simplifications and boundary conditions.
:LABEL: Subtopic

name: Boundary layers
description: Boundary layers: Thin regions adjacent to solid surfaces in which viscous effects produce strong velocity gradients and influence momentum, heat, or mass transfer. In Viscous Flow, the focus is on concept-level scope: the defining mechanism, properties, constraints, and application criteria; curricular context is recorded in Concept_Category and Typical_Modules.
:LABEL: Subtopic

name: Pelton and Francis turbines
description: Pelton and Francis turbines: Hydraulic turbine types represented by Pelton impulse turbines and Francis reaction turbines for converting water energy into shaft power. In Hydraulic Turbines, the focus is on pelton jet/bucket interaction; Francis runner, pressure change, head, flow rate, efficiency and operating range.
:LABEL: Subtopic

name: Centrifugal pumps
description: Centrifugal pumps: Rotodynamic pumps that impart energy to a fluid primarily through the action of a rotating impeller, converting mechanical energy into fluid pressure and head. In Pumps, the focus is on concept-level scope: the defining mechanism, properties, constraints, and application criteria; curricular context is recorded in Concept_Category and Typical_Modules.
:LABEL: Subtopic

name: Grashof's law
description: Grashof's law refers to a kinematic criterion for planar four-bar linkages relating link lengths to the possibility of continuous rotation of at least one link. In Mechanisms, the focus is on shortest/longest/other link lengths, S+L ≤ P+Q criterion and limiting cases.
:LABEL: Subtopic

name: Instantaneous centers
description: Instantaneous centers: Points or centers in planar rigid-body motion about which the relative velocity between two bodies is instantaneously equivalent to rotation. In Velocity/Acceleration Analysis, the focus is on relative motion, Kennedy's theorem, velocity relationships and construction methods.
:LABEL: Subtopic

name: Cam displacement diagrams
description: Cam displacement diagrams: Graphs relating follower displacement, velocity, acceleration or related motion variables to cam angle or time. In Cams, the focus is on follower motion laws, rise/dwell/return, simple harmonic/cycloidal/polynomial motion and motion continuity.
:LABEL: Subtopic

name: Epicyclic gear trains
description: Epicyclic gear trains: Gear arrangements in which one or more gears rotate about axes that themselves move relative to a fixed frame. In Gears, the focus is on sun, planet, ring and carrier elements; relative motion; speed ratios and torque relationships.
:LABEL: Subtopic

name: Friction in machine mechanisms
description: Friction in machine mechanisms: Resistance to relative motion between contacting machine components, affecting forces, power loss, wear and motion. In Friction, the focus is on dry/sliding friction, rolling resistance, friction laws, lubrication effects and efficiency implications.
:LABEL: Subtopic

name: Fins
description: Fins: Extended surfaces used to increase heat-transfer area and enhance heat transfer between a solid and an adjoining fluid. In Conduction, the focus is on fin geometry, conduction within the fin, convection boundary condition, efficiency/effectiveness and temperature distribution.
:LABEL: Subtopic

name: Free/forced convection
description: Free/forced convection: Heat transfer between a surface and moving fluid driven respectively by buoyancy or by externally imposed fluid motion. In Convection, the focus is on natural/free convection, forced convection, boundary layers, dimensionless correlations and heat-transfer coefficients.
:LABEL: Subtopic

name: Blackbody radiation
description: Blackbody radiation: Thermal radiation idealization for a surface that absorbs all incident radiation and emits the maximum possible radiation at a given temperature. In Radiation, the focus is on blackbody emissive power, Stefan-Boltzmann law, spectral distribution and radiative exchange assumptions.
:LABEL: Subtopic

name: Log Mean Temperature Difference (LMTD)
description: LMTD: Log-mean temperature difference, a mean temperature-driving-force measure used in heat-exchanger analysis when the temperature difference varies along the exchanger. In Heat Exchangers, the focus is on concept-level scope: the defining mechanism, properties, constraints, and application criteria; curricular context is recorded in Concept_Category and Typical_Modules.
:LABEL: Subtopic

name: Mass diffusion and transfer coefficients
description: Mass diffusion and transfer coefficients: Transport of chemical species caused by concentration gradients and the coefficients used to relate mass-transfer flux to a driving concentration difference. In Mass Transfer, the focus is on fickian diffusion, concentration gradients, molecular diffusivity, convective mass transfer and dimensionless correlations.
:LABEL: Subtopic

name: Flywheels
